scenarios.name: healthy_unit_shows_fan_heat_only
scenarios.description: The pin this rule exists to keep clear: a draw-through unit with the heating coil shut still warms its air by dTSF = 1 °C crossing the supply fan, so sat − mat = +1.0 °C in every healthy OS#2-#4 hour. The 4.1623 °C threshold carries the fan-heat term precisely so this reads healthy forever; without it every healthy AHU in the fleet would alarm

scenarios.name: rise_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge: sat − mat = 4.1623 °C exactly, the composed sqrt(eHCET² + eHCLT²) + dTSF allowance. `riseBig` is a strict `>`, so a rise sitting precisely on the allowance reads healthy — G36's `≥` would report it (see Deviations)

scenarios.name: rise_just_over_threshold
scenarios.description: Threshold edge, other side: sat − mat = 4.2623 °C clears the strict comparison on the first tick and the alarm asserts one alarm_delay (1800 s) later

scenarios.name: heating_valve_leaking_during_free_cooling
scenarios.description: OS#2 on a mild morning: the economizer mixes to 16 °C and the air reaches the supply sensor at 23 °C with the heating valve commanded 0%. Take the fan's 1 °C back out and the coil is adding about 6 °C to air the economizer was brought in to cool — hot water flowing through a valve that reports itself shut, which is exactly the leak AHU-FC-050 is structurally blind to

scenarios.name: mat_sensor_reading_low
scenarios.description: Same 6 °C signature in a season when the hot-water plant is locked out and the valve has been verified shut: no coil can be adding heat, and the mixed-air sensor is what is wrong. The rule reports the contradiction; G36 lists both sensor errors ahead of the valve in its diagnosis order for this reason

scenarios.name: transient_clears_before_alarm_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: a 7 °C rise persists for 1200 s while hot water standing in a just-closed coil gives up its residual heat, then SAT settles back to mat + fan heat. Anything shorter than alarm_delay never reaches the operator

scenarios.name: fault_clears_on_recovery
scenarios.description: A sustained 7 °C rise alarms at 1800 s; the leaking valve is isolated at t = 3000 and SAT falls back to mat + fan heat. `TrueDelay` has no off-delay, so the alarm drops on that tick

scenarios.name: oscillating_rise_never_alarms
scenarios.description: An electric heating stage short-cycling on a 10-minute period swings the rise between 7 °C and 1 °C. Its mean is well outside the allowance and G36's 5-minute rolling average would report the fault, but persistence restarts on every compliant tick, so this rule stays silent — the limit of substituting TrueDelay for averaging (see Deviations)
